Fixed workflow rails:
[RL-0006] Read outcomes and exclusions only from the _protocol JSON: targets in _protocol['targets'], dropped columns in _protocol['excluded_columns'], the group in _protocol['group_column'], task details in _protocol['task']. The Brief in this order is a different object; never index _protocol with Brief keys. If a needed key is missing, raise an error that lists the available top-level keys instead of guessing a nested path.
[RL-0007] Define the feature columns once: every column of the frozen table except the targets, the excluded columns and the group column, and except key-like columns: text codes or integer sequences whose values are all distinct and carry no measurement. Continuous measurements are never identifiers, however many distinct values they have. Use exactly that list in every step, and never let a target or excluded column reach a fitted transformer or model.
[RL-0011] Saved transformers from earlier steps may already contain the earlier preprocessing. Before combining them, check isinstance(obj, Pipeline) and obj.named_steps to see whether the later object includes the earlier one; build on the most complete saved pipeline that accepts the raw feature DataFrame and append only the new estimator. Never place a saved pipeline after a step it already contains, and never pass NumPy arrays to a transformer that selects columns by name. Inspect feature_names_in_ for each loaded object and preserve its exact input columns and order. A saved selector may already wrap preprocessing: use that selector as the only frontend, or chain preprocessing once before a bare selector. Never feed derived or renamed columns back into a raw-column frontend. Saved preprocessing and models accept the raw feature columns (the engine refuses others when they are saved): call a loaded model on frame[list(model.feature_names_in_)] and do not require it to be a Pipeline.
[RL-0012] Summary tables have one type per column: use NaN, not empty strings, for values that do not apply, or put numeric and categorical summaries in separate columns. Keep at most 50 rows and 12 columns; for wide summaries, place variables in rows and statistics in columns.
[RL-0013] Keep each script short and direct, about 120 lines or fewer: loop over columns instead of repeating blocks, no commented-out alternatives, no long docstrings, no restating of these instructions. A complete short script is better than an elaborate one that is cut off.
[RL-0014] When repairing, read the error type and message in the diagnostics first and change the smallest part of the script that causes it; keep the approach, inputs and outputs. A message about specifying columns with strings on non-dataframes means an array reached a name-based transformer (see RL-0009 and RL-0011). A KeyError on a JSON key means a guessed structure; use the keys the file has. Messages starting with 'MLCA:' state an engine rule; comply, do not work around it.
[RL-0015] When the training table has more than 100000 rows, avoid methods whose cost grows with the square of the row count (full silhouette, kernel SVMs, pairwise distances, t-SNE, agglomerative clustering) and prefer linear models with saga or SGD solvers, HistGradientBoosting or MiniBatchKMeans. Every fit_record call still uses all training rows; compute expensive diagnostics that fit nothing on a fixed-seed subsample of at most 10000 rows and print its size.
[RL-0021] There is no outcome in this project: never treat any column as a label or count its categories as one. Choose the cluster count only from internal criteria (silhouette, Davies-Bouldin, Calinski-Harabasz, stability). Scale features before distance-based methods. Compute silhouette with sample_size at most 10000 and a fixed random_state. Required per-row outputs hold the assigned cluster for each row_id.
[RL-0026] Persist the full row-preserving feature transformation contract, not just an estimator fitted after transient DataFrame mutations. Parsing, derived features, column selection and ordering needed later must be reproducible by the saved importable pipeline. Learned transforms fit only on the frozen training rows. Deterministic table preparation may precede the split only through a declared prepared-data artifact. Later steps pass the declared source feature schema to the saved pipeline, never assume derived columns already exist in a freshly loaded partition. Inspect fitted input names; do not invent missing columns or fit replacement preprocessing during evaluation.
[RL-0027] Before combining saved transformers, compare their feature_names_in_. Two saved objects that both expect the raw feature columns were fitted side by side, not in sequence; never chain one after the other, because the second then receives transformed output instead of the raw columns. Use only the one the step needs, normally the most complete, or place both side by side on the raw feature DataFrame (FeatureUnion). Chain an object after another only when its feature_names_in_ match the other's output names.
Read the declared _protocol JSON: use _protocol['task']['primary_metric'], _protocol['targets'], _protocol['excluded_columns'] and the declared outcome columns. primary_metric is nested inside task, not a top-level key. Binary threshold selection is validation-only; multiclass uses macro one-vs-rest ROC AUC without a binary threshold. Never fit after test exposure.
Train and val inputs hold at most 10000 rows each (a fixed-seed sample of larger partitions); use them as given and print the row counts.

Previous script: import mlca_runtime
import json
import pickle
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

mlca_runtime.set_seed(42)
inputs = mlca_runtime.inputs()
protocol = json.loads(inputs["_protocol"].read_text())

for key in ["targets", "excluded_columns", "group_column", "task"]:
    if key not in protocol:
        raise KeyError(f"Missing protocol key {key}; available top-level keys: {sorted(protocol.keys())}")
task = protocol["task"]
if "primary_metric" not in task:
    raise KeyError(f"Missing task['primary_metric']; available top-level keys: {sorted(protocol.keys())}; task keys: {sorted(task.keys())}")
targets = list(protocol["targets"])
excluded = list(protocol["excluded_columns"])
group = protocol["group_column"]
primary_metric = task["primary_metric"]

train = pd.read_parquet(inputs["train"])
def is_key_like(s, name):
    if s.nunique(dropna=True) != len(s):
        return False
    if s.dtype.kind in "OUS" or str(s.dtype) in ("object", "string", "category"):
        return True
    return any(tok in str(name).lower() for tok in ["id", "code", "index", "row", "key", "serial"])

feature_cols = [c for c in train.columns if c not in set(targets + excluded + [group]) and not is_key_like(train[c], c)]

def load_pkl(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        return pickle.load(f)

model_src = "07_model_train_baseline_SWTMFPFT/model.pkl"
alt_src = "08_model_train_alternative_XQ00QFTN/alternative_model.pkl"
val_src = "09_validate_score_validation_H8CSBPBR/validation_metrics.csv"
cand_src = "07_model_train_baseline_SWTMFPFT/cluster_candidates.csv"
model = load_pkl(inputs[model_src])
alt = load_pkl(inputs[alt_src])
pre = load_pkl(inputs["05_preprocess_fit_preprocessing_1E8V578C/preprocessor.pkl"])
sel = load_pkl(inputs["06_features_retain_features_Y7PF8JJ2/selector_all.pkl"])

def final_est(obj):
    if hasattr(obj, "named_steps") and obj.named_steps:
        return list(obj.named_steps.values())[-1]
    return obj

final = final_est(model)
def output_names(n):
    for o in [sel, pre, model]:
        if hasattr(o, "get_feature_names_out"):
            try:
                names = list(o.get_feature_names_out())
                if len(names) == n:
                    return names
            except Exception:
                pass
    for o in [model, sel, pre]:
        if hasattr(o, "feature_names_in_"):
            names = list(o.feature_names_in_)
            if len(names) == n:
                return names
    return None

nclusters = getattr(final, "n_clusters", np.nan)
if hasattr(final, "cluster_centers_"):
    centers = np.asarray(final.cluster_centers_, dtype=float)
    nfeat = centers.shape[1]
    names = output_names(nfeat) or [f"feature_{i}" for i in range(nfeat)]
    top_feature = names[int(np.argmax(centers.std(axis=0)))]
    nclusters = centers.shape[0]
elif hasattr(final, "feature_importances_"):
    vals = np.asarray(final.feature_importances_, dtype=float)
    nfeat = len(vals)
    names = output_names(nfeat) or [f"feature_{i}" for i in range(nfeat)]
    top_feature = names[int(np.argmax(np.abs(vals)))]
elif hasattr(final, "coef_"):
    vals = np.asarray(final.coef_, dtype=float)
    vals = np.abs(vals).mean(axis=0) if vals.ndim > 1 else np.abs(vals)
    nfeat = len(vals)
    names = output_names(nfeat) or [f"feature_{i}" for i in range(nfeat)]
    top_feature = names[int(np.argmax(vals))]
else:
    nfeat = len(feature_cols)
    top_feature = feature_cols[0] if feature_cols else "unknown"
    try:
        support = np.asarray(sel.get_support())
        if len(feature_cols) == len(support) and support.any():
            top_feature = feature_cols[int(np.where(support)[0][0])]
    except Exception:
        pass

def metric_value(df, name):
    for c in df.columns:
        if name in c.lower():
            s = pd.to_numeric(df[c], errors="coerce").dropna()
            if len(s):
                return float(s.iloc[0])
    lc = {c.lower(): c for c in df.columns}
    for key in ["metric", "name", "metric_name"]:
        if key in lc:
            for vc in ["value", "score", "val"]:
                if vc in lc:
                    mask = df[lc[key]].astype(str).str.lower().str.contains(name)
                    if mask.any():
                        s = pd.to_numeric(df.loc[mask, lc[vc]], errors="coerce").dropna()
                        if len(s):
                            return float(s.iloc[0])
    return np.nan

def best_candidate(df):
    scol = next((c for c in df.columns if "silhouette" in c.lower()), None)
    if scol is None:
        return np.nan, np.nan
    s = pd.to_numeric(df[scol], errors="coerce")
    if not s.notna().any():
        return np.nan, np.nan
    idx = s.idxmax()
    kcol = next((c for c in df.columns if any(t in c.lower() for t in ["cluster", "n_clusters", "k"])), None)
    return (df.loc[idx, kcol] if kcol else np.nan), float(s.loc[idx])

val = pd.read_csv(inputs[val_src])
cand = pd.read_csv(inputs[cand_src])
sil = metric_value(val, "silhouette")
best_k, best_s = best_candidate(cand)

def num4(x):
    if isinstance(x, (int, np.integer)):
        return int(x)
    if isinstance(x, (float, np.floating)):
        return float(f"{x:.4g}") if np.isfinite(x) else np.nan
    return x

rows = []
def add(section, item, value, source):
    if value is None:
        value = np.nan
    if isinstance(value, str) and value == "":
        value = np.nan
    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple, dict)):
        value = str(value)
    rows.append({"section": section, "item": item, "value": num4(value), "source": source})

add("model", "selected_model_file", model_src, model_src)
add("model", "estimator", type(final).__name__, model_src)
add("model", "pipeline_steps", " > ".join(model.named_steps.keys()) if hasattr(model, "named_steps") else np.nan, model_src)
add("model", "alternative_estimator", type(final_est(alt)).__name__, alt_src)
add("model", "n_clusters", nclusters, model_src)
add("model", "top_feature", top_feature, "interpretation.csv")
add("inputs", "feature_columns", ", ".join(feature_cols), "train.parquet")
add("inputs", "n_input_features", len(feature_cols), "train.parquet")
add("inputs", "n_model_features", nfeat, model_src)

params = final.get_params(deep=False) if hasattr(final, "get_params") else {}
preferred = ["n_clusters", "init", "n_init", "max_iter", "tol", "algorithm", "random_state", "metric", "linkage", "affinity", "batch_size", "assign_labels"]
hp = []
for k in preferred:
    if k in params:
        hp.append((k, params[k]))
for k, v in params.items():
    if len(hp) >= 12:
        break
    if k not in [x[0] for x in hp] and isinstance(v, (str, int, float, bool, type(None), np.integer, np.floating)):
        hp.append((k, v))
for k, v in hp:
    add("hyperparameters", k, v, model_src)

add("validation", "primary_metric", primary_metric, "_protocol")
add("validation", "validation_silhouette", sil, val_src)
add("validation", "best_candidate_k", best_k, cand_src)
add("validation", "best_candidate_silhouette", best_s, cand_src)
add("validation", "candidate_rows", len(cand), cand_src)

for item, text in [
    ("no_outcome", "No outcome or label column is present; clusters are unsupervised segmentation summaries."),
    ("internal_metric", "Validation evidence is internal silhouette only and may not reflect external validity."),
    ("no_refit", "The frozen model and preprocessing were described without fitting or refitting on validation rows."),
    ("scaling", "Distance-based clustering uses scaled features, so top_feature reflects standardized model space."),
    ("top_feature", "top_feature is derived from the frozen estimator's dispersion or importance and is not causal."),
    ("split", "Validation evidence is limited to the declared validation partition used as given."),
]:
    add("limitations", item, text, "interpretation.csv")

out = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["section", "item", "value", "source"])
mlca_runtime.save_table(out, "interpretation.csv", caption="Frozen clustering model interpretation")
mlca_runtime.record_fact_candidate("top_feature", top_feature, source="interpretation.csv")

print("features", len(feature_cols))
print("model", type(final).__name__, "clusters", nclusters)
print("validation_silhouette", num4(sil))
print("top_feature", top_feature)
print("wrote interpretation.csv")
